svg.title: The unseen side
svg.desc: The unseen side is the side every commander is measured against: the scripted commander with its orders hidden from its own pilots. The first box, The scripted commander, is labelled orders shown. An azure box labelled scripted commander sends three solid azure order lines with open arrowheads to three azure darts on the right. Its pilots see each order and fly it. The second box, The unseen side, is labelled the same commander, orders hidden. It repeats the commander and three darts in the same positions in ember. Three dashed ember order lines stop before a short vertical wall labelled hidden. No line reaches a pilot. It gives orders by the same rules, but none reach its pilots. They see exactly what a ship with no order sees, and fight on their own judgment. It still launches its craft and steers its carrier as the script does. The final box, How a commander is measured, shows an azure box labelled commander being tested with three azure darts against an ember box labelled unseen side with three ember darts. There are no order lines in this match strip. About 0.50: its orders are worth no more than none. Clearly above 0.50: its orders help. The number is the share of matches it wins against the unseen side, a draw counting half. A commander that gives no orders and launches as the script does scores about 0.50.
